title: Global services stop before their world and editor consumers
summary: Application shutdown deinitializes jobs and logging before editor and world teardown even though world unload/destructors discard queues and asynchronous/system destruction paths can still use both services.

evidence.note: JobManager and LoggingSystem stop before Editor::UnInitialize and WorldManager::ClearWorlds.
World teardown calls DiscardJobQueue and destroys systems after the global services have stopped.

impact: Shutdown can enter invalid service state, lose cancellations/logs, or dereference already-torn-down job infrastructure.
recommendation: Define explicit shutdown phases: stop producers, cancel and join world work, tear down editor/worlds, unload resources while backends live, then stop jobs/logging/platform/filesystem.
validation: Repeated create-run-exit under ASan with jobs active

title: Suspended atomic is not initialized
summary: Application::m_bSuspended is a default-initialized std::atomic_bool with no C++17 constructor/in-class value; reading before SetSuspended is indeterminate.

evidence.note: Getter can read an uninitialized atomic.
Constructor initializes exit state but not suspended state.

impact: Dormant undefined state can surface when suspension is integrated into the loop/platform lifecycle.
recommendation: Initialize the atomic to false in-class or in the constructor.
validation: Construct Application and assert IsSuspended is false

title: Deferred world stack operations dereference empty stacks
summary: PushWorld uses back() without requiring an existing world; PopWorld can pop the last world and immediately use back() on the empty vector.

evidence.note: Deferred callback dereferences m_Worlds.back without an empty guard.
After pop_back, the callback dereferences m_Worlds.back even when the removed world was the last one.

impact: Valid zero/one-world transitions can crash when deferred operations are applied.
recommendation: Validate stack state inside each deferred callback and define empty push/pop semantics.
validation: Queue multiple push/pop operations before SwapWorlds

title: Asynchronous world load captures raw world and application state
summary: World asynchronous load work captures this and accesses serializer, logging, and manager state without a lifetime token or join barrier.

evidence.note: Worker/completion lambdas retain raw world/application relationships.

impact: World replacement or application shutdown can race parse/completion work and produce use-after-free or cross-thread engine mutation.
recommendation: Parse into owned immutable job results, gate completion with a world generation/lifetime token, mutate the world only on the main thread, and join before teardown.
validation: Rapidly open/replace/exit during large world loads under ASan/TSAN

title: World initialization constructs runtime dummy objects to force linkage
summary: World::Initialize constructs volatile temporary Entity and pathfinding types solely to prevent optimization/link stripping, causing allocations/destruction and consuming a global entity ID.

evidence.note: Five temporary runtime objects are explicitly marked Do not remove.
Every temporary Entity increments EntityIdCounter and allocates a Transform.

impact: Every world initialization performs hidden work and perturbs serialized/runtime ID sequences.
recommendation: Use explicit RTTR/linker registration anchors or build references and remove dummy construction.
validation: Verify registrations directly and assert no extra entity ID is consumed by World::Initialize

title: Tag removal is ineffective and hierarchy cycles are accepted
summary: RemoveTag omits erase after remove_if; SetParent can accept this or an ancestor/descendant cycle and recurse through hierarchy repair.

evidence.note: remove_if result is discarded.
No explicit self or ancestor-cycle rejection precedes recursive mutation.

impact: Removed tags remain visible and malformed hierarchies can recurse indefinitely or corrupt parent/child state.
recommendation: Use erase-remove and reject self plus all descendant parents before any mutation.
validation: Self-parent, two-node cycle, and deep ancestor cycle tests

title: Routine removal invalidates iteration and completed tasks leak
summary: BehaviorScript::StopRoutine erases a vector during range iteration; ScriptSystem erases completed Routine and Delegate pointers without deleting them.

evidence.note: Deletes and erases while continuing range-for iteration.
Completed routine pointer is erased without destruction.
Completed delegate pointer is erased without destruction.

impact: Stopping routines can invoke undefined iterator behavior; ordinary completion leaks heap objects.
recommendation: Adopt unique_ptr ownership and iterator-returning erase or deferred removal with exactly-once destruction.
validation: Complete many routines/delegates under leak sanitizer

title: Loaded entity ID counter is restored off by one
summary: The serializer compares against highest loaded ID plus one but assigns the counter to highest, allowing the next generated entity to reuse an existing loaded ID.

evidence.note: EntityIdCounter is set to highest instead of highest + 1.

impact: ID collisions can misresolve links and break entity identity after loading a world.
recommendation: Set the counter to max(current, highest + 1) using checked arithmetic.
validation: Load IDs 1..N then create entity and assert ID N+1

title: Event subscriptions have weak identity and incomplete removal
summary: Event subscriptions are identified by a class-pointer hash, duplicates are allowed, and operator-= removes only the first matching subscription. There is no RAII connection token.

evidence.note: Subscription/removal storage is pointer-hash based and invocation copies the callback list.

impact: Reinitialization can leave duplicate or stale callbacks; object address reuse makes identity fragile. Copy-on-invoke does make mutation during the active call safe.
recommendation: Return unique connection tokens and disconnect by token/RAII; make duplicate policy explicit.

title: Unsigned worker-count arithmetic can create an unbounded thread loop
summary: hardware_concurrency()-1 and maxThreads-3 are evaluated with unsigned arithmetic; CPU reports of zero or fewer than four can wrap to enormous values.

evidence.note: hardware_concurrency result is decremented without a zero guard.
Unsigned subtraction is compared with > 0 and used as a loop bound.

impact: Startup can attempt billions of worker allocations/threads, hanging or exhausting the process.
recommendation: Compute in a checked signed type, clamp to an explicit minimum/maximum, then convert to size_t.
validation: Inject reported hardware counts 0 through 8 and assert bounded worker count

title: Job queues are deleted before workers are joined
summary: Deinitialize signals kill and deletes active queues while worker objects/threads still exist and can scan those queues; the same mutex does not guard the whole lifetime transition. Shelved queues are omitted.

evidence.note: Queue deletion precedes JobThread destruction/join.
Thread join occurs only when worker objects are later destroyed.

impact: Shutdown can race a worker read against freed JobQueue memory; shelved queues/jobs leak.
recommendation: Close submissions, signal cancellation, join workers, then delete/drain all active and shelved queues under one lifetime protocol.
validation: Repeated shutdown with busy/shelved queues under ASan/TSAN

title: Job exception and cancellation completion semantics are unsafe
summary: Job::Run executes without an exception boundary. Queue destruction deletes pending jobs without guaranteeing Canceled or Finish, so completion semantics silently disappear.

evidence.note: Run is invoked on the worker with no catch-to-result boundary.
Pending job ownership is destroyed without a defined exactly-once callback contract.

impact: A worker exception terminates the process; canceled work can leave flags/locks/resources permanently owned.
recommendation: Catch exceptions into failed results and define exactly-once Finish/cancel cleanup with RAII job ownership.

title: Polling waits and registry access can stall or race
summary: Workers and WaitForJob poll at 10 ms; WaitForJob has no timeout and retains unrelated finished jobs until the target appears. Queue registry reads are not consistently synchronized against discard.

evidence.note: Infinite polling loop temporarily owns unrelated completions.
Registry lifetime is not uniformly locked against deletion.

impact: Main-thread callbacks are delayed, waits can hang forever, and queue lookup can race deletion.
recommendation: Use condition variables/futures with timeouts, continue processing unrelated completions, and lock or handle-own the registry.

title: Logging collections and events are shared without synchronization
summary: Worker error paths can mutate log vectors/maps and invoke events while the editor/main thread reads the same state; LoggingSystem has no threading barrier.

evidence.note: Record collections and callbacks are modified/read without a mutex or main-thread queue.
Editor consumes logging state/events on the main thread.

impact: Concurrent errors can corrupt containers, race callbacks, or target partially torn-down UI state.
recommendation: Queue immutable records from workers for main-thread consumption or protect all state and document callback threading.
validation: Multi-worker log flood while opening/closing console under TSAN

title: Generic JSON validation accepts partial schema and empty buffers
summary: FromJson uses AND instead of OR for two required members, then indexes whichever member is absent; it lacks object/string checks. Empty file vectors are passed through &buffer[0].

evidence.note: Exactly one missing required member falls through to invalid access.
Empty readBuffer uses element-zero address.

impact: Empty or partially malformed settings/data can assert, crash, or invoke undefined behavior.
recommendation: Require every member with OR logic, validate all JSON types, reject empty input, and use data()+size safely.

title: World and prefab deserialization trust unvalidated JSON and component types
summary: World/prefab paths do not consistently check parse errors, member types, arrays, or lengths. An unknown RTTR component becomes null and is passed into Entity::AddComponent.

evidence.note: Empty buffer and parse/schema failures are not comprehensively rejected.
Prefab parser follows the same unchecked pattern.
Unregistered type can return null to AddComponent.

impact: Malformed/outdated/unregistered content can assert, dereference null, partially mutate a world, or allocate from attacker-controlled values.
recommendation: Validate a versioned schema transactionally before construction and report unknown types with path/context.
validation: Fuzz RapidJSON entry points under ASan

title: Serialization APIs report success without successful completion
summary: World/entity save ignores filesystem write results; generic ToJsonFile returns on write failure without closing its handle. SerializeWorldAsync is a no-op that never invokes its callback, and FromJsonFile cannot receive semantic conversion failure because FromJson is void.

evidence.note: Write return is not propagated.
Write return is not propagated.
Function body never completes callback.
Failure exit leaves file handle open.

impact: Callers can believe persistence succeeded, wait forever for callbacks, and leak handles.
recommendation: Return structured results through every layer, close handles with RAII, and guarantee async completion exactly once.

title: Numeric and container conversions are not range/shape safe
summary: uint16 uses signed to_int16; associative key dispatch repeats IsUint and omits IsUint64; vector conversion indexes fixed elements after only checking IsArray.

evidence.note: Unsigned 16-bit values above 32767 are converted through signed 16-bit.
Duplicate IsUint branch misses uint64 key handling.
Vector arrays are indexed without exact length/element validation.

impact: Values corrupt silently or malformed containers trigger invalid RapidJSON access/asserts.
recommendation: Centralize checked numeric casts and validate exact container lengths, element types, and legal JSON object-key conversion.

title: Deferred link resolution leaks state across load transactions
summary: ResolveWorldLinks returns early when connection work is empty without clearing old prefab-ID remaps; partially loaded chunk/world links can be cleared before targets become available.

evidence.note: Early return bypasses remap clear performed only at the normal end.

impact: Later loads can inherit stale ID mappings or permanently lose unresolved cross-chunk references.
recommendation: Scope connection/remap data to a load transaction, clear on every exit with RAII, and retain unresolved links until terminal success/failure.
validation: Sequential prefab loads with first load having no links

title: World version compatibility is encoded as an undocumented numeric gap
summary: Compatibility admits versions at/above 1.10 and at/below 1.02 while rejecting 1.03 through 1.09; intent/migration behavior is not expressed as an explicit table.

evidence.note: Version predicates create a discontinuous supported range.

impact: Content owners receive a generic failure and future maintainers can accidentally broaden/narrow compatibility.
recommendation: Document a supported-version/migration table and test every boundary with actionable errors.

title: VOX load reports success after parse/open failure
summary: VoxModel::Load continues after Read fails and unconditionally sets loaded/returns true. The config handle is checked as a boolean even though INVALID_FH is UINT_MAX/nonzero; its heap buffer is leaked.

evidence.note: Failure is freed but execution continues to success state; invalid config handle passes truthiness check.

impact: Failed/corrupt assets enter the resource cache as loaded with invalid frames/audio state and can crash later baking or destruction.
recommendation: Load transactionally; compare handles to INVALID_FH; own config bytes; publish loaded state only after complete success.

title: Solid voxel accessor exposes total count to compact arrays
summary: VoxFrame::GetSolidVoxelCount returns m_uiVoxelCount rather than m_uiSolidVoxelCount, so baker/stamper can iterate beyond compact solid color/position arrays. Fully transparent frames also retain inverted min/max bounds.

evidence.note: Accessor returns the wrong member.
Returned count sizes/iterates bake data.
Returned count drives stamp reads.

impact: Transparent voxels cause uninitialized/out-of-bounds reads; transparent-only frames can turn invalid fitted dimensions into huge allocations.
recommendation: Return the solid count, model empty bounds explicitly, and reject/handle empty frames before fitted allocation.

title: VOX free/reset/reload ownership is not idempotent
summary: Free does not clear frames, null arrays, or reset audio/mapper/loaded flags; Reset returns at the first null frame and skips later frames.

evidence.note: Owned records/state remain in containers after release.
Early return prevents reset of subsequent frames.

impact: Reload/destructor paths can double-free/release stale backend resources or retain dangling frame records.
recommendation: Make frames RAII-owned, clear every container/pointer/flag/handle, and make Free safe to call repeatedly.
validation: Multiple frames with an empty first/middle frame under ASan

title: VOX parser count and chunk boundaries are not validated
summary: A signed file count is assigned to uint32 before a negative check, enabling huge allocation. Parsing assumes XYZI follows SIZE and uses frames.back(); read/seek results and chunk remaining lengths are not comprehensively enforced.

evidence.note: Untrusted counts/chunk ordering feed allocations and frame access.

impact: Malformed VOX data can allocate excessively, access an empty frame list, or read beyond chunk/file boundaries.
recommendation: Parse into checked signed/64-bit temporaries, cap all products, validate chunk grammar and remaining bytes, and fail without publishing partial state.

title: Hollow frame creation aliases ownership and uses empty-vector element zero
summary: CreateHollowFrame begins with a shallow copy of a frame containing owning pointers and can take &newData[0] when newData is empty. Palette conversion also uses a strict-aliasing pointer cast.

evidence.note: Owned pointer fields are copied before selected replacements; empty data address is unsafe.

impact: Empty/hollow assets can invoke undefined behavior and copied ownership can double-free if an early path/destructor observes aliases.
recommendation: Construct a fresh frame with explicit ownership and use data()+size plus memcpy/bit-safe palette conversion.

title: Manual resource reference counts can underflow or race deletion
summary: Reference counts are unsigned, non-atomic, and manually balanced. Over-release wraps instead of reaching zero; last release synchronously deletes through an event while raw users may remain.

evidence.note: Unsigned decrement detects only exact zero and is not synchronized.
Release callback erases/deletes the object synchronously.

impact: Over-release leaks, cross-thread access races, and last-release reentrancy can invalidate callers.
recommendation: Use an owned handle/control block or enforce main-thread-only resource access; detect underflow and make eviction ownership explicit.

title: Resource path filtering and sound backend initialization are fragile
summary: Resource file filtering uses the first dot instead of the final extension; SoundReference::m_pAudioContext has no default initializer and can be read by destruction after incomplete setup.

evidence.note: First-dot parsing misclassifies dotted directory/file names.
Raw backend pointer is not initialized in declaration.

impact: Valid asset paths are omitted/misclassified and failed construction paths can read indeterminate backend state.
recommendation: Use filesystem final-extension parsing and initialize backend pointers to nullptr.

title: Spherical voxel destruction accepts unsafe sizes and leaks on early exit
summary: Radius is rounded/cast to unsigned without finite/nonnegative/range checks; diameter and cube products can overflow or allocate excessively. Missing chunks return after raw allocations and m_pIntegrityJob is dereferenced without a null guarantee.

evidence.note: Unchecked radius/products, raw arrays, leaking early return, and unconditional integrity job access share one path.

impact: Invalid/game-driven radius or unavailable chunks can exhaust memory, corrupt indexing, leak, or crash.
recommendation: Validate/cap radius, use checked size_t multiplication and vectors, skip missing chunks safely, and make integrity scheduling optional/owned.
validation: Negative, NaN, infinity, zero, and huge radius

title: Integrity worker reads live voxel/chunk storage without a snapshot
summary: IntegrityJob traverses VoxelGrid while physics/chunk/main-thread code mutates non-atomic voxel containers and chunk-volume pointers; teardown can invalidate the grid during a scan.

evidence.note: Worker directly reads shared grid/chunk state.
Main-thread mutation/residency uses ordinary containers and raw pointers.

impact: Data races can produce inconsistent island results, out-of-bounds access, or use-after-free.
recommendation: Run against an immutable/versioned snapshot or hold an explicit read lifetime lock and join before grid/chunk destruction.
validation: Destruction plus chunk churn stress under TSAN/ASan

title: Integrity job generations can clobber ownership during pause/resume
summary: Resume can install a new integrity job while the prior completion callback remains pending; the old callback unconditionally sets m_pIntegrityJob to null. Destruction requests stop but does not prove join before captured lifetime ends.

evidence.note: Completion callback clears the shared pointer without generation comparison.
Cancellation is requested without a demonstrated synchronous join.

impact: The live job becomes untracked and can later touch a destroyed system/grid; future destruction can null-dereference or fail to cancel it.
recommendation: Use generation-tagged owned job handles, compare before clearing, and synchronously cancel/join on pause/destruction.
validation: Destroy immediately after resume under ASan

title: Voxel grid construction and coordinate-zero boundaries are unsafe
summary: Create can divide by zero, overflow 32-bit dimension products, and truncate non-divisible dimensions. WorldToGrid/rounding excludes coordinate zero through strict >0 checks.

evidence.note: Dimensions/products are trusted.
Boundary checks reject zero coordinates.

impact: Invalid settings can crash/underallocate; valid boundary voxels are reported out-of-grid.
recommendation: Require positive/divisible dimensions, use checked size_t products, and define inclusive/exclusive coordinate bounds.
validation: All six grid faces including zero

title: Voxel grid fast paths assume chunk residency
summary: GetChunk/cell/voxel fast routes dereference a chunk-volume slot without proving it is non-null/resident. The fully-out-of-bounds low-side predicate combines axes so single-axis low exclusions fall through inconsistently.

evidence.note: Fast path uses m_ChunkVolumes[chunkArrPos] without a residency guard.

impact: Queries during load/unload transitions can crash or traverse unexpected partial ranges.
recommendation: Represent residency explicitly, null-check every access route, and correct per-axis rejection.
validation: Concurrent/rapid chunk residency churn with boundary queries under ASan

title: Zero-capacity particle linked list indexes invalid storage
summary: ParticleLinkedList(0) indexes element zero, underflows loop bounds, and accesses size-1.

evidence.note: Constructor assumes capacity is at least one.

impact: A zero-size setting or caller causes immediate invalid memory access.
recommendation: Support an explicit empty state or reject zero before any indexing.
validation: Construct capacities 0, 1, and N under ASan

title: Platform and Vulkan initialization failures do not stop the frame loop
summary: Platform::Initialize returns void and ignores backend failure. VKRenderContext can mark backend-ready, fail later command-engine setup, and return without undoing partial state.

evidence.note: Window/render/audio initialization results are not propagated to Application.
Partial command-engine failures leave backend-ready/allocated state.

impact: Startup proceeds into Clear/Present with missing/null required render objects and crashes far from the original failure.
recommendation: Return a structured result, build transactionally, unwind reverse-order on failure, and never enter the loop unless required capabilities are ready.
validation: Inject failure at every backend/command-engine stage and assert clean exit/no leaks

title: Required render objects use inserting map lookups then dereference null
summary: Named buffers, passes, and command engines are frequently fetched with operator[] and immediately dereferenced, so a missing registration inserts null and causes a delayed crash.

evidence.note: Required objects are accessed by string/map and assumed present.
Getter patterns expose inserting lookup behavior.

impact: Typos or partial initialization mutate the registry and convert actionable configuration errors into null dereferences.
recommendation: Use find/at with contextual failure or typed owned members/IDs and validate all required registrations during initialization.
validation: Remove/misspell each required object and assert startup error rather than crash

title: Voxel and camera consumers lack complete bounds/null handling
summary: RenderContext::GetVoxel(raw index) has no bounds check; RenderSystem coordinate getter checks only negatives. RenderSystem and AudioSystem still dereference the main camera, and Application ignores Present's boolean failure.

evidence.note: Raw index is trusted.
Upper coordinate bounds are not checked.
Main camera is dereferenced in subsystem paths.
Present result is discarded.

impact: Transient camera-less worlds, bad coordinates, or persistent swapchain failure can crash or loop silently.
recommendation: Centralize checked voxel addressing, make cameras optional across all systems, and recover/exit/report persistent presentation failure.

title: Voxel stamp origin and transform allocation edges are unsafe
summary: VoxelStamp starts lastPosition at origin and skips a legitimate first origin voxel. Stamp/bake accepts nonfinite, zero, or huge scale/rotation settings; solid-count times rounded-scale can overflow before per-voxel diagnostics.

evidence.note: Origin is used as a sentinel instead of an explicit hasLast flag.
Allocation product precedes complete transform/range validation.

impact: Origin content disappears and invalid transforms can allocate excessively or overflow buffer sizing.
recommendation: Use an explicit hasLast value, validate/cap finite transforms, and checked-multiply allocation sizes.

title: Dynamic text is passed as an ImGui format string
summary: Texture paths, FPS strings, entity names, and runtime TextRenderer content are passed directly to ImGui Text/TextWrapped as the format argument.

evidence.note: texturePath.c_str() is a format string.
fpsString.c_str() is a format string.
Entity name is a format string.
Runtime text is a format string.

impact: Content containing percent directives can read nonexistent varargs, crash, or expose/corrupt memory depending on format support.
recommendation: Use TextUnformatted or a constant "%s" format for every dynamic string.
validation: Render names/textures/text containing %s, %p, %n, and %% under ASan

title: Ground texture indexing can underflow or divide by zero
summary: Ground-texture coordinate math uses unsigned subtraction and modulo by texture dimensions without requiring nonzero dimensions; out-of-range Z can underflow and produce incorrect tiling.

evidence.note: Unsigned coordinate/modulo expression trusts dimensions.

impact: Zero-size textures divide by zero; some out-of-range coordinates return incorrect colors.
recommendation: Validate dimensions and normalize signed coordinates with explicit modular/bounds semantics.

title: Chunk async state can stick and jobs capture unstable owners
summary: Load/unload/render flags are set before a JobQueue is proven available; missing queues leave state permanently in progress. Jobs capture raw chunk/system/item pointers and references to vector-held groups that teardown/reallocation can invalidate.

evidence.note: Loading state precedes queue availability and lambdas capture raw owners.
Unloading has the same transition/lifetime shape.
Rendering flag and &group capture depend on vector/world lifetime.

impact: Chunks/groups can remain stuck forever or completion can use freed/moved memory during world/chunk churn.
recommendation: Acquire queue and owned task state before transition, clear every flag on all exits, capture stable IDs/results, and cancel/join before owner mutation.
validation: Group-vector growth while work runs under ASan/TSAN

title: Chunk RLE decoder does not validate record framing or output bounds
summary: Decode does not require encoded bytes to be a multiple of seven and does not prove cumulative runs stay within the destination volume.

evidence.note: Malformed record sizes/runs feed direct output writes.

impact: Truncated or corrupt persisted chunk data can read past input or write past output.
recommendation: Validate framing, each run, checked cumulative length, exact expected output, and owner/color semantics before committing decoded data.

title: Chunk bounds clamp one past the valid grid and underflow small worlds
summary: Several coordinates clamp to numChunks instead of numChunks-1; unsigned negative tests are dead. World offset subtracts three from unsigned chunk counts, underflowing worlds smaller than the 3x3 streaming window.

evidence.note: Inclusive clamp and unsigned subtraction produce invalid chunk coordinates.
Same last-index clamp error appears in chunk calculations.

impact: Edge/small worlds can request invalid chunks, compute huge offsets, or divide/query outside configured space.
recommendation: Use checked signed coordinates, last-valid clamps, and explicit behavior for worlds smaller than the near-field footprint.

title: Chunk encoding forces large allocation churn
summary: Each encode reserves 10 MB and then shrink_to_fit, discarding capacity that could be reused.

evidence.note: Fixed large reserve and shrink occur per unload.

impact: Streaming churn creates avoidable allocator pressure, stalls, and memory fragmentation.
recommendation: Estimate from input or reuse bounded scratch capacity across jobs; benchmark representative movement.
validation: Allocator/profile comparison across repeated 3x3 chunk movement

title: Far-field asset path collection trusts JSON string schema
summary: FarFieldBaker model-path collection calls RapidJSON GetString without proving object/member/string types.

evidence.note: World/content JSON is traversed without complete type validation.

impact: Malformed/outdated world content can assert before the otherwise strong far-field bounds/NaN validation runs.
recommendation: Reuse a validated world schema and return contextual errors before collecting/baking paths.

title: Async path group work captures a dangling range variable reference
summary: ChunkGrid schedules group-field work with a lambda capturing &group, where group is the range-for variable whose reference lifetime/rebinding does not extend safely to asynchronous execution.

evidence.note: Worker lambda captures the loop variable by reference.

impact: Work can write through a dangling reference or update the wrong group, causing memory corruption or invalid path fields.
recommendation: Capture a stable owned pointer/ID by value only after guaranteeing container lifetime, or compute from copied inputs and apply results on main-thread completion.
validation: Multiple groups with delayed worker execution under ASan
Container growth while phase is pending

title: Pathfinding jobs have no backpressure or owner join barrier
summary: Agent work is enqueued every tick and captures raw grid/group/agent/transform state. ChunkGrid destruction does not cancel/join it; m_iGridLocks crosses threads as a plain int, and ChunkBuilderJob::Canceled does not release its constructor-acquired lock.

evidence.note: One job per tick can accumulate without an in-flight guard.
Destructor repairs links but does not join jobs capturing this.
Cancellation omits grid-lock release performed by normal completion.

impact: Work can pile up, race state, leave the grid permanently locked, or access destroyed pathfinding objects.
recommendation: Allow one generation per phase, snapshot inputs, apply owned results on main thread, make lock cleanup terminal-path RAII, and join on destruction.
validation: Slow workers plus high frame rate
Destroy grid/world with jobs active under ASan/TSAN

title: Pathfinding phases advance without successful work and node fields never reset
summary: The grid phase increments unconditionally even when interval/queue conditions skip the phase. Density, discomfort, and velocity are accumulated through splats, but Node::reset has no call site.

evidence.note: Phase advances regardless of whether its action ran/completed.
Reset exists but no first-party call was found.

impact: Pipeline phases consume stale/missing prerequisites and crowd fields grow frame over frame.
recommendation: Advance on successful phase completion only and reset or replace per-generation node fields before splatting.
validation: No queue and rebuild-interval scheduler trace

title: Path neighbor and required-component checks dereference the wrong or null object
summary: Reverse connection logic reads node.m_connections instead of neighbourNode.m_connections. Pathfinder writes defaults for missing body/collider and then dereferences them; other fixed-tick branches also use a missing body.

evidence.note: Reverse edge check indexes the current node's connections.
Null defaults are followed by dereference.
Some flag combinations dereference physicsBody without a surviving guard.

impact: Navigation topology can be asymmetric/wrong and entities missing expected components crash.
recommendation: Read reverse state from the neighbor and return/disable navigation when required physics components are absent.
validation: Pathfinder with no body, no collider, and all flag combinations

title: Crowd flow math overwrites settings and produces stale or unstable vectors
summary: Awake/Start overwrite reflected tuning values; separation divides by squared distance twice and before a zero check; X and Z both store into m_flockVelocityX; empty-neighbor paths preserve stale velocity. Separate height/velocity selection uses signed rather than absolute distance and topo speed extrapolates below minimum.

evidence.note: Serialized/reflected tuning is replaced by hardcoded values.
Distance, component assignment, selection, and clamping inconsistencies occur across flow methods.

impact: Configured behavior is ignored and agents can receive NaN, fourth-power falloff, stale, or axis-corrupted velocities/heights.
recommendation: Preserve configuration, centralize epsilon-safe vector math, reset empty results, assign axes correctly, use absolute nearest selection, and clamp topology inputs.
validation: Golden numeric tests at zero/epsilon/near/far distances

title: Pathfinding shared state, timers, and zero-vector math lack isolation
summary: Workers read groups/agents/nodes while main-thread mutation is possible and unordered maps may mutate concurrently. testTimer is a cpp-global shared by every grid. Zero radii and normalize(zero) can divide by zero or emit NaN.

evidence.note: Timer is global rather than per grid.
Normalization/radius math lacks complete epsilon validation.

impact: Multiple grids interfere; races and NaNs can make navigation nondeterministic or corrupt shared structures.
recommendation: Snapshot worker inputs, confine mutable maps to one thread, make timers instance state, and validate/epsilon-guard radii and normalization.

title: Specific-player input branches index player vector with enum count
summary: Multiple branches set playerControllerIndex to BMT_PLAYERCONTROLLERS (value 9) instead of deriving the selected controller; the vector is currently sized to one.

evidence.note: Specific-controller operations index an out-of-range constant.

impact: Using a concrete player binding type deterministically accesses outside m_PlayerControllers.
recommendation: Map concrete enum to enum-BMT_PLAYERCONTROLLER1, validate against size, and centralize the conversion.
validation: Every BindingMapType route with 0, 1, and configured N controllers under ASan

title: Axis bindings are registered but not dispatched correctly
summary: Axis callbacks are stored, but ProcessInputBindings invokes only actions. A specific-player axis route calls ProcessBindingAxis on the global handler rather than the selected player controller.

evidence.note: Axis callback storage exists.
Only action processing is invoked.
Specific-player axis dispatch targets the global map.

impact: Axis-driven gameplay callbacks do not fire or read the wrong controller.
recommendation: Dispatch axes each frame through the resolved handler and share tested controller-routing logic with actions.
validation: Global, aggregate, and specific-player axis callbacks and values

title: Modifier and binding-map state transitions are incorrect
summary: Modifier logic treats only RELEASED as satisfied and breaks after the first modifier, acting like OR rather than all-held. Destroying the active map leaves its pointer dangling. Default-map setter updates an inner map while getter returns unchanged context state.

evidence.note: Modifier loop status and early break do not implement an all-held chord.
Active map is erased without fallback/null update.
Setter/getter use different authoritative storage.

impact: Shortcuts fire under wrong key states, active map access can use freed memory, and default-map API lies.
recommendation: Define all-modifier semantics, transition active map before erase, and keep one authoritative default name.

title: Controller lifecycle and player-handle swaps leave stale callbacks
summary: Mouse/keyboard Uninitialize deletes the singleton returned by Get without resetting initialized flags; gamepad globals also persist. InputHandler::SwapPlayerHandle rebinds actions only, so axes remain on the old controller while destruction unbinds from the new controller.

evidence.note: Singleton deletion does not reset static lifecycle state.
Same lifecycle pattern.
Only action handles are rebound.
Axis cleanup targets current/new controller rather than the old registration.

impact: Reinitialization can use freed singleton state and old axis callbacks retain a dangling InputHandler capture.
recommendation: Use explicitly owned/resettable controller instances and symmetrically unbind/rebind actions plus axes.
validation: Swap player then destroy handler and emit old/new axis

title: Input enums, modifier matching, and callback mutation permit invalid access
summary: InputKeyStatus is used directly as an array index although IKS_NONE=-1. Modifier comparison is asymmetric/subset-based. Callbacks can remove entries from the unordered_map currently being iterated.

evidence.note: Public status value indexes handler arrays without validating IKS_NONE.
Stored/requested modifier set comparison is asymmetric.
Callbacks execute during unordered-map traversal.

impact: Invalid status can index before storage, modifier variants can match unexpectedly, and self-removal may invalidate iteration.
recommendation: Translate/reject invalid enums, compare normalized modifier sets, and dispatch from a stable snapshot or defer mutations.

title: Public player-controller range exceeds allocated capacity
summary: BindingMapType exposes eight concrete player-controller values while InputContextNew initializes one controller.

evidence.note: Player controller vector is sized to one.
API declares eight player slots plus aggregate values.

impact: Callers cannot infer supported player count and most declared routes are unusable even after the indexing bug is fixed.
recommendation: Define one configured maximum and derive storage, validation, and public API behavior from it.

title: Audio playlist empty and clear operations index invalid elements
summary: Play clamps index to size() rather than size()-1, PlayNext takes modulo zero when empty, and ClearAudioFiles loops <= size while removals shrink the vector.

evidence.note: Clamp permits one-past-end.
Empty list modulo zero.
Inclusive loop mutates its bound/container.

impact: Normal empty/end-of-list operations can crash, divide by zero, or skip/release the wrong entries.
recommendation: Define empty behavior, clamp to last valid index, and clear via a safe ownership-aware loop/container clear.
validation: Empty, one-item, last-item, and repeated clear

title: Audio source replacement dereferences failed or null references
summary: SetFilePath and SetSoundReference obtain channels and read reference loop data before proving load/reference success.

evidence.note: Failed/null loaded reference reaches GetLoopStart after channel acquisition.
Reference is dereferenced before the null check.

impact: Missing/failed sound assets or explicit null replacement can crash and leave partially replaced channel/reference state.
recommendation: Load/validate a temporary reference first, then atomically swap; make null an explicit clear/stop route.

title: FMOD error paths continue with null systems or channels
summary: Initialization failure handling is conditional in debug/editor behavior; Release can continue with a null system. PlaySound/PlayBGM log errors then dereference null channels. StopBGM can retain a reference when channel is null; destruction does not consistently release BGM state; IsPlaying trusts its channel.

evidence.note: Failure is not uniformly terminal across build modes.
Logged failure can continue into channel use.
Null channel early return can retain reference/state.
Channel is dereferenced without a null guard.

impact: Audio/device/resource failure can crash Release builds or leak/stale BGM references.
recommendation: Make every FMOD result control flow in every build and own system/channel/reference state with idempotent RAII transitions.

title: Audio system retains camera and source lifetime assumptions
summary: PostTick dereferences the main camera; OnComponentDestroyed stops and erases AudioSource state but does not clear raw m_pBGM or m_pNextBGM when they point to that source.

evidence.note: Listener update assumes a main camera.
BGM raw pointers are not invalidated with source destruction.

impact: Camera-less worlds crash and later BGM ticks can use a destroyed AudioSource.
recommendation: Make listener optional and clear/transition BGM handles synchronously on component destruction.
validation: Destroy current/next BGM source during fade under ASan

title: FMOD 3D velocity is populated from position
summary: Set3DParameters constructs both FMOD position and velocity vectors from the position argument.

evidence.note: Velocity parameter is not used for the FMOD velocity vector.

impact: Doppler/spatial behavior is physically incorrect.
recommendation: Populate velocity from the velocity argument and cover with a mock/backend assertion.
validation: Distinct position/velocity values passed to mocked FMOD channel

title: Free-list allocator can allocate past blocks and corrupt live memory
summary: Allocate selects/uses the first node even when too small, split remainder math omits metadata/alignment costs, and m_pFreeListHead is not correctly advanced when root is split/consumed. Free can write through a head pointing inside a live allocation.

evidence.note: Search termination, fit, split, and head update invariants are broken.
Insertion through stale head can overwrite active data.

impact: Any real use can overlap allocations or corrupt allocator/user memory.
recommendation: Replace with a proven address-ordered free-list algorithm and checked block-layout invariants before enabling production use.

title: Linear and stack allocators miscompute alignment and initialization
summary: Linear allocation aligns relative to the whole-buffer end rather than current front and its capacity check can omit debug header/footer; root initialization can succeed with null memory. Parent StackAlloc does not initialize front and aligns an allocation end rather than returned pointer.

evidence.note: Initialization and layout math do not guarantee aligned in-bounds user storage.
Parent/front setup and user-pointer alignment are incomplete.

impact: Returned pointers can be misaligned, debug metadata can overflow buffers, and parent-backed stack allocations can use invalid front state.
recommendation: Derive checked layouts from current front with uintptr_t alignment, include all metadata in capacity, and fail null initialization.

title: Pool allocator parent mode and block layout are corrupt
summary: Parent-backed initialize does not build the free list. Object stride is not aligned after the first block, capacity ignores initial padding, and debug Free pushes the user pointer rather than block base.

evidence.note: Parent mode reaches allocation without initialized free-list blocks.
Stride/padding/debug free pointer violate block-base invariants.

impact: Parent allocation fails immediately; other modes can return misaligned objects or corrupt the free list on reuse.
recommendation: Use an aligned block base/stride, initialize every block in every mode, and recover the exact block base on free.

title: Allocator base polymorphism and debug footer calculations disagree
summary: BaseAlloc lacks a virtual destructor despite polymorphic design; InvalidateBlock applies alignment adjustment to footer addressing while IsValidBlock does not.

evidence.note: Destructor and debug metadata helpers do not provide safe polymorphic/consistent behavior.

impact: Polymorphic deletion can skip derived destruction and debug invalidation writes the wrong marker, undermining diagnostics.
recommendation: Add a virtual destructor or prohibit base deletion and share one footer-address helper.
validation: Validate/invalidate same block at multiple alignments

title: Broken custom allocators appear dormant rather than safe
summary: Allocator translation units are built, but no first-party production use was found outside their implementations and legacy unit tests.

evidence.note: Reference search found implementation/test use, not active engine allocation call sites.
Tests exist but are not wired into current CMake/CTest.

impact: Current exposure is lower, but severe latent corruption can be activated later without CI warning.
recommendation: Remove/quarantine the allocators or repair them and activate sanitizer/property tests before adoption.
validation: CMake/reference audit preventing new untested use

title: POSIX file modes, write results, and stream position are incorrect
summary: FlagsToOpenMode checks READ before RDWR, so combined flags select a read-only mode and an RDWR-create branch is unreachable. Write ignores fwrite; GetFileSize rewinds rather than restoring the original position; long seek/tell limits large files.

evidence.note: Bit-subset ordering misroutes RDWR combinations.
Short/error write is reported as FSR_OK.
Caller file position is not restored.

impact: Read/write files open incorrectly, persistence can silently truncate/fail, callers read from the wrong position, and >2GB files are unsafe on some platforms.
recommendation: Match exact flag combinations, check writes, preserve position, and use 64-bit platform seek/tell.

title: Async filesystem requests race handle and caller-owned lifetime
summary: Async reads capture raw this and caller pInfo; file maps/FILE operations are not synchronized with Close/Deinitialize. Deinitialize closes handles but leaves map entries populated; global handle generation is unsynchronized.

evidence.note: Async read, close, map, and teardown share raw handle state without a join/lock protocol.
File handle/request ownership is raw and global/static.

impact: Close/shutdown can race active I/O, caller request info can dangle, and stale map entries permit double close/use of invalid FILE pointers.
recommendation: Own request inputs/results, serialize operations per handle, cancel/join before close, clear the registry, and synchronize opaque handle generation.

title: Player preference deletion leaks and typed getters dereference failed casts
summary: DeleteAll/DeleteKey erase raw Pair pointers without delete. A key read under the wrong requested type dynamic_casts to null and is immediately dereferenced; setters silently ignore mismatches.

evidence.note: Raw pair ownership is erased without destruction.
dynamic_cast result is trusted.

impact: Preference churn leaks memory and type mismatches crash instead of returning a recoverable error.
recommendation: Store values/unique_ptr, return typed optional/error, and define replacement versus rejection on type mismatch.
validation: Read same key as every wrong type

title: Persisted preference parsing and static lifetime are not failure safe
summary: Double and date/time preference conversion uses throwing stod/stoll without handling; static singleton/state and raw preference pointers have no explicit shutdown reset.

evidence.note: Persisted string conversion exceptions can leave application load paths.
Static state owns raw pairs without a deterministic application-lifetime reset contract.

impact: Malformed preference data can terminate startup and repeated application lifecycles can leak/stale state.
recommendation: Use checked parsing with contextual fallback and explicit Initialize/Shutdown ownership.
validation: Two application lifecycles in one process

title: Fixed timer counts multiple steps but executes one callback
summary: ChronoGameTimer consumes N fixed intervals and advances counters N times, then invokes the fixed callback once. ResetElapsedTime does not reset Chrono last-time, second counter, elapsed tick, or conversion remainder.

evidence.note: Catch-up loop and callback count diverge.
Base reset omits derived Chrono sampling state.

impact: After stalls, simulation time/counters advance without matching physics steps; reset can include blocked/loading time in the next delta.
recommendation: Execute one bounded callback per consumed step with a max catch-up/drop policy and reset all derived timing/remainder state.
validation: Inject 0.5s stall at 60Hz and assert callback/counter policy

title: Zero timing and dimensional settings are not semantically rejected
summary: A zero fixed-step target makes the catch-up loop non-terminating; zero frame limit changes callback behavior. Related physics/chunk/window dimensions reach downstream division/allocation without centralized validation.

evidence.note: Loop relies on a positive target elapsed time.
Deserialized settings are not comprehensively range-normalized before construction.

impact: A malformed Settings.vgs can hang startup/frame processing or trigger divide-by-zero/overflow in several systems.
recommendation: Validate and normalize all configuration once before subsystem creation with safe ranges and diagnostics.

title: DateTime constructors and parsing do not establish complete state
summary: DateTime(int64_t) initializes current time but not UTC/public broken-down fields, so ToUTC can expose default/stale data. Parse lets stoll exceptions escape. The working tree contains a preserved user portability edit in this header.

evidence.note: Constructor does not populate all representations.
Invalid numeric input is not converted to a result/error.

impact: Timestamp-constructed objects can report inconsistent UTC fields and malformed persisted values can throw through callers.
recommendation: Use one canonical fully initialized representation, derive fields in every constructor, and return checked parse errors; revalidate after the user edit is finalized.

title: ORBIS FPS logging uses a dangling pointer as a format string
summary: The ORBIS branch takes c_str from a temporary concatenated string and then passes that dangling pointer directly as printf's format.

evidence.note: Temporary string dies before printf and dynamic content is the format argument.

impact: ORBIS builds have use-after-lifetime and format-string undefined behavior every FPS print.
recommendation: Keep the string alive and use a constant format or print the integer directly.
validation: Compile/run ORBIS branch with sanitizers or platform equivalent

title: Clearing command history leaves freed pointers in the container
summary: CommandManager::Clear deletes every command but does not clear m_pCommands; later destructor/undo/redo can double-delete or use freed memory. A maximum history of zero calls front on an empty vector.

evidence.note: Deleted pointer vector is retained.
Zero max history is not handled before front access.

impact: Normal editor history clearing/reconfiguration causes deterministic use-after-free or double deletion.
recommendation: Store unique_ptr, clear the vector after deletion (or simply clear owned handles), and define zero as disabled history.

title: Undo commands retain stale targets and contain uninitialized/index-underflow paths
summary: Commands hold raw Entity/Component/Transform/World pointers that can outlive targets. EditorEntityCommand::m_pNewCreatedEntity is uninitialized before fallback dereference; IncrementEntityName decrements size_t below zero for all-digit names.

evidence.note: Pointer lacks a default initializer.
Fallback dereference and reverse suffix scan trust pointer/index state.
History records raw runtime targets.

impact: World unload/target deletion, command fallback, or all-digit names can use freed/uninitialized memory or underflow iteration.
recommendation: Resolve stable IDs at execution or invalidate history on target/world destruction, initialize all fields, and parse suffixes with bounded indices.
validation: Names empty, alphabetic, mixed, and all digits under ASan

title: Entity commands stage only direct children
summary: Editor entity add/duplicate command adds the root and direct children to the world, while serializer reconstruction is recursive, so nested descendants are omitted from active staging.

evidence.note: Only one child level is added.
Serializer has recursive hierarchy handling, demonstrating expected depth.

impact: Deep duplicated/prefab hierarchies can exist in inconsistent active/world ownership and undo states.
recommendation: Recursively stage the complete hierarchy with one ownership path.

title: Editor teardown retains event subscriptions and stale map entries
summary: Editor::Initialize subscribes to WorldManager and RenderContext events; UnInitialize does not unsubscribe. Released/deleted button and texture values remain in maps, so reinitialization duplicates callbacks and stale pointers.

evidence.note: World/render subscriptions capture Editor.
Subscriptions and maps are not comprehensively disconnected/cleared.

impact: Shutdown/reinitialize events can invoke a partially destroyed editor or dereference released UI resources.
recommendation: Use RAII connection tokens, disconnect before owned view/resource teardown, and clear every pointer map.
validation: Emit world/render events after teardown under ASan

title: Editor world-pop traversal can dereference rend and queue duplicate pops
summary: Reverse traversal increments and then dereferences when the editor world is absent or the stack bottom is exhausted; deferred behavior permits multiple pops to be queued before the stack changes.

evidence.note: Reverse iterator and deferred PopWorld assumptions are not bounded.

impact: Unusual world stack ordering/absence can crash or remove more worlds than intended at the next swap.
recommendation: Use a bounded search, never dereference rend, and record one pending validated transition.
validation: Editor world absent, only world, bottom, middle, and repeated frame transition

title: Performance panel divides by zero and labels rates as timings
summary: Performance display derives values from FPS counters without guarding zero and labels CPU/GPU FPS-derived quantities as timings.

evidence.note: Zero counters and unit labels are not handled.

impact: Startup/missing samples show infinities/NaNs and mislead profiling decisions.
recommendation: Represent unavailable samples explicitly and display measured duration with correct units.

title: Deserialized settings lack centralized semantic validation
summary: Settings are loaded structurally but positive timing steps, nonzero dimensions, checked allocation products, and backend-compatible ranges are not normalized before dependent systems initialize.

evidence.note: Settings are accepted directly before JobManager/Platform/world construction.
Individual setters clamp some display values, but there is no complete ValidateAndNormalize boundary.

impact: Malformed/manual Settings.vgs values make timer, voxel-grid, chunk, rendering, and allocation defects reachable early.
recommendation: Add one contextual ValidateAndNormalize pass before subsystem construction and use checked dimension products.

title: CI does not build the full engine, game, or editor
summary: GitHub Actions builds the Vulkan bring-up target and a targeted RTTR Settings compile check on Ubuntu, not the full engine/game/editor link surfaces.

evidence.note: Configure relies on default bring-up behavior plus VOXAGINE_CHECK_RTTR.
Full engine is an optional path separate from current CI coverage.

impact: Manifest drift, platform-port failures, and most reviewed code can break without pull-request feedback.
recommendation: Add full game and editor builds on supported platforms plus a manifest/source drift check.
validation: CI matrix compiles/link game Debug/Release and editor Debug/Release

title: Legacy engine tests are not integrated with CMake or CTest
summary: GoogleTest sources exist for allocators, math, physics, pathfinding, and RTTR, but root CMake has no active test executable, enable_testing, or add_test route.

evidence.note: Test files are present.
No CTest registration for UnitTesting was found.

impact: Known high-risk areas have tests that neither compile nor run, allowing rot and regressions.
recommendation: Port/register the tests in CMake/CTest, update them for current types, and run Debug/Release in CI.
validation: ctest --output-on-failure reports and runs all engine tests

title: No sanitizer, fuzz, or static-analysis gate covers critical boundaries
summary: No automated ASan/UBSan/TSAN, fuzzing, or static-analysis configuration was found for parser, allocator, chunk, job teardown, or pathfinding concurrency paths.

evidence.note: Only ordinary Debug/Release bring-up builds run.
No current fuzz/stress/sanitizer targets are registered.

impact: Memory corruption and races documented in this review are unlikely to be caught before runtime/manual testing.
recommendation: Add ASan/UBSan, TSAN where supported, clang-tidy/static analysis, JSON/VOX/RLE fuzzers, and lifecycle/chunk/path stress tests.
validation: CI publishes sanitizer/fuzz/static-analysis results with zero findings

title: Explicit source manifests can silently omit new translation units
summary: Engine source files are intentionally enumerated in cmake manifests to control portability; repository presence alone does not make a new cpp compile.

evidence.note: Header comment documents manual maintenance.
Target consumes explicit manifests rather than a source glob.

impact: New implementations can appear complete locally/review-wise while never entering a target.
recommendation: Compare eligible first-party cpp files with manifests in CI and require an explicit exclusion list.
validation: Manifest-drift script fails on an unlisted temporary cpp fixture

title: Packed voxel owner identity has a finite non-recycling slot budget
summary: The pulled owner sidecar reserves sentinels and permits 65,533 distinct static owners; slots intentionally never recycle to prevent stale identity reuse.

evidence.note: uint16 owner representation and sentinel policy define the cap.

impact: Very long sessions or unusually high owner churn can exhaust identity capacity even if active owner count is lower.
recommendation: Instrument exhaustion and preserve non-reuse, or introduce generation-tagged wider/recyclable handles before changing semantics.
validation: Allocate owner slots to cap and assert deterministic diagnostic/failure

title: Voxel color lookup reaches the end without a value
summary: VoxFrame::GetVoxelColor returns a color only when a compact solid position matches; an empty voxel or inconsistent position array reaches the end of a non-void function.

evidence.note: MSVC C4715 in the full editor Release build confirms the missing terminal return.

impact: Calling the accessor for a non-solid coordinate has undefined behavior and can return arbitrary color data.
recommendation: Return an explicit transparent/empty value (or optional/result) when no solid voxel matches and validate coordinates against the compact representation.
validation: Lookup solid and empty coordinates in empty/mixed frames

title: Full editor build is successful but not warning-clean
summary: The verified full Release editor/game build emits first-party warnings: DXC deprecated effect-style declarations and implicit vector truncations, DataHook macro redefinitions, a compiler-unproven terminal return in InputContextNew::GetAxisValue, and the actionable VoxFrame::GetVoxelColor missing return tracked separately.

evidence.note: DXC G891B5F2B effect syntax warning; similar declarations occur in other shaders.
DXC implicit truncation warnings; other shader truncations are also reported.
Empty macros are redefined when USE_DATAHOOKS is unconditionally enabled.
MSVC C4715 because total behavior is expressed as separate conditional returns without an explicit fallback; existing input findings cover the unsafe concrete-player branch.

impact: Warnings hide new regressions and prevent adopting warnings-as-errors; some represent real undefined behavior while others obscure intent.
recommendation: Resolve current warnings, make intentional conversions/declarations explicit, and introduce a staged warning budget followed by /WX and DXC warning enforcement for first-party code.
validation: Full game/editor Release builds with zero first-party compiler and shader warnings
